purpose: Provide type-specific diagram extraction and rendering prompts for MiMo body-region PPT generation. MiMo should not invent diagram rules from scratch; the pipeline should select the closest diagram type and inject its contract.

execution_model.reason: Different diagrams optimize different semantics. A universal prompt makes MiMo mix flow, architecture, evidence, matrix and dashboard rules, causing drift, overlap and generic layouts.
execution_model.fallback_policy: If classification confidence is low, use semantic_infographic, not generic card grid.

global_contract.role: You are a senior PPT information-graphics designer and technical diagramming expert. Output must look like a competition-grade presentation diagram, not a web widget, report table, or AI sketch.

output.render_step: HTML fragment only. Root node must be .mimo-body-root. Inline style and SVG are allowed. No script.

slide_density.content_page: Use focus statement + main diagram/evidence + 2-4 supporting labels. Avoid one diagram plus one sentence. Avoid speaker-script paragraphs.
slide_density.visible_text_target_cn: 70-170 Chinese chars for normal pages; 120-240 for dense technical/evidence pages.
slide_density.focus_text: 8-18 Chinese chars, visible on slide, not a repeat of the outer title.

geometry.safe_bounds: Body internal elements: left/right inset about 1.8%, top/bottom inset about 3.5%. SVG viewBox internal graphic inset 6%-8%.
forbid: more than 5 freeform paths unless they are part of a simple chart
text placed on top of lines or arrows

typography.line_rule: Short labels only. If text does not fit, reduce words before reducing font size.

style.color_rule: Choose colors from the deck theme. Use one dominant accent, one secondary accent, tinted neutral surfaces and clear contrast.
style.shape_rule: Use rectangles, rounded rectangles, diamonds, circles, bands and rings deliberately. Cards are support elements, not the default main structure.
style.depth_rule: Use line weight, scale, transparency and spacing for hierarchy. Do not rely on decorative gradients alone.

render_contract_v2.purpose: A precise construction contract for first-pass MiMo diagram rendering. This should prevent table-like architecture, drifting lines, tiny text, crowded nodes and generic card grids before audit/repair.

canvas.root: .mimo-body-root must fill the body region, overflow hidden, no root padding, no root background, no large inner whiteboard.
canvas.safe_area: All visible diagram elements stay inside x=1.8%-98.2%, y=3.5%-96.5%. SVG internal viewBox keeps 6%-8% inset.
canvas.occupied_area: Main diagram should occupy 62%-82% of body area on core diagram pages. If it occupies less than 58%, enlarge the main structure before adding decoration.
canvas.grid: Use an 8px visual grid. Node x/y/w/h should align to 8px increments when using CSS pixels.

composition_strength.principle: The first pass must create a strong PPT composition, not merely a correct diagram. One visual object must dominate the body region.
composition_strength.main_visual_ratio: Architecture, evidence_chain, data_flow and flowchart pages: main visual target 65%-82% of body area; minimum acceptable 58%.
composition_strength.focal_hierarchy: Use 1 dominant focus, 2-4 support elements, and 1 conclusion/result accent. Avoid equal-weight nodes unless the diagram type is explicitly matrix.
composition_strength.scale_contrast: Dominant node/result/value should be 1.35x-1.8x larger or visually stronger than support nodes.
composition_strength.empty_space_rule: Whitespace must wrap the main visual; it cannot appear as unused top/side blank. If a large blank area remains, expand the main diagram or add a controlled conclusion rail.
composition_strength.result_emphasis: Every technical diagram needs a visible destination/result node, seal, stage or output band; it should not be a small tag.

typography.node_title_px: 18-24px, weight 700-820, max 10 Chinese chars per line, max 2 lines.
typography.node_body_px: 14-16px, weight 500-650, max 16 Chinese chars per line, max 2 lines.
typography.overflow_policy: Never solve fitting by using text below 13px. First shorten copy, then wrap to 2 lines, then move detail to speaker notes.

node_geometry.primary_node: Width 190-300px, height 84-132px. Use for claim/result/core layer.
node_geometry.tag_node: Width 72-132px, height 26-40px. Use for source, metric or protocol tags.
node_geometry.corner_radius: Large structural bands 6-10px; small tags 4-8px; avoid 18px+ web-card radius.
node_geometry.stroke: 1.2-2px normal, 2.4-3.5px emphasis. Do not use hairlines below 1px.
node_geometry.inner_padding: 12-18px for nodes. Text baseline must not touch borders.

spacing.node_gap: Horizontal/vertical gap 24-48px. Dense diagrams may go to 18px only if no connector crosses text.
spacing.lane_gap: Layer/lane gap 16-28px, but bands must stay visually connected by bus/axis.
spacing.callout_gap: Callouts sit 12-24px from the shape they explain.
spacing.top_empty_limit: Do not leave more than 18% of body height empty above the main diagram on content pages.

connectors.arrow_head: 8-12px. Arrowheads must not overlap node text or borders.
connectors.routing: Prefer straight, orthogonal or one gentle curve. Max one dashed feedback line.
connectors.label_rule: Connector labels never sit on the line. Place labels in small tags beside the connector or attach to nodes.
connectors.crossing_policy: No crossing connectors. If crossing would happen, switch to lanes, stack or hub-spoke.

table_and_matrix_style.allowed_when: Only comparison_matrix, risk_matrix or metric_dashboard may use table/matrix grammar.
table_and_matrix_style.visual_table: If using a matrix, make headers/bands/axes explicit; use 2-4 columns and 3-5 rows; cell text max 12 Chinese chars.
table_and_matrix_style.not_allowed: Architecture, data_flow, evidence_chain and flowchart must not become report tables or row lists.
table_and_matrix_style.matrix_strokes: Outer boundary 1.5-2px; inner separators 1px with 25%-45% opacity; highlighted cell/band 2-3px.

special_case_policy.too_many_nodes: If >6 nodes, group into 3-4 clusters/layers and show representative labels.
special_case_policy.long_labels: If label >12 Chinese chars, split into title + tiny evidence tag or rewrite to verb-object phrase.
special_case_policy.missing_metrics: Do not fabricate precise numbers. Use qualitative levels, source tags or relative arrows.
special_case_policy.unclear_order: If order is unclear, use matrix/hub-spoke instead of forcing a false flow.
special_case_policy.dense_evidence: If evidence sources >4, make a proof wall with 3 visible anchors + one folded source strip.
special_case_policy.small_body_region: Reduce support labels before shrinking diagram; keep main visual readable.

architecture.layout: Use system boundary + 3-4 full-width layers or tower. Layers are broad stacked bands with depth and a dominant data bus, not table rows. Each band must contain modules plus an explicit data bus/flow crossing layers.
architecture.composition: The system boundary/layer-stack-stage must occupy 65%-80% of the body area. The data bus must be the visual spine, and the application/output node must be the clear destination.
architecture.sizes: Layer band height 84-128px; system boundary inset 14-24px; module chips 86-150px by 28-42px; output/application node 1.45x-1.8x larger than module chips.
architecture.connectors: One main data-flow/bus 6-8px, vertical or horizontal, with 2-4 short branch arrows. No more than 8 visible branch connectors. Branch arrows 2-3px.
architecture.anti_table: Do not draw four plain rows with tiny chips at the right. If the result looks like a table, convert rows into layered bands with a central bus crossing them and a large destination/output node.
architecture.special: If modules are many, show 2-3 module chips per layer and group the rest as '+N 能力'.

data_flow.layout: Use pipeline band, swimlane or funnel-to-output. Separate source, processing, storage/model and output zones.
data_flow.sizes: Step nodes 150-220px by 70-100px; output node 220-320px by 96-132px; lane labels 78-120px wide.
data_flow.connectors: One continuous main path 4-6px. Quality-control tags attach to steps with 1.5-2px short leader lines.
data_flow.special: If feedback exists, use exactly one dashed feedback arrow outside the main path, opacity 45%-65%.

flowchart.layout: Use 3-6 main steps in horizontal, vertical, swimlane or loop form. Decision nodes are diamonds and max 2.
flowchart.sizes: Step nodes 150-230px by 68-108px; decision diamond 92-128px; start/end nodes may be pill shapes.
flowchart.connectors: Straight or orthogonal arrows 2.2-3.2px, arrowhead 8-12px. Branch labels sit beside the branch, not on the line.
flowchart.special: If branches exceed 2, collapse them into an exception lane instead of drawing a complex tree.

evidence_chain.layout: Start with a large claim/value stage, then 2-4 evidence anchors, then result/action seal. Use proof wall, stage, bracket or rail; never upload boxes.
evidence_chain.composition: The claim/value stage must be the largest object and occupy 30%-45% of the body width or 18%-28% of body area. Evidence anchors are subordinate and must not become equal cards. Result seal must be visually attached to the stage or rail.
evidence_chain.sizes: Claim/value stage 360-620px by 110-190px; proof nodes 160-230px by 72-108px; result seal 150-220px by 88-132px and at least 1.25x stronger than a proof node.
evidence_chain.connectors: Evidence connects by one rail/bracket/axis. Use max 1 main arrow or rail at 5-7px and max 3 short proof leaders at 1.5-2.5px.
evidence_chain.visual_finish: Claim stage should feel like a presentation stage plate with layered gradient, thin highlight edge, soft glow and one bold internal arrow. Result seal should use concentric ring/check/value badge treatment. Evidence rail should use a continuous axis with ticks/brackets and proof connectors.
evidence_chain.legibility: Result seal and proof-node text must remain high contrast. Text contrast >=4.5, result seal background alpha >=0.88, proof-node colored/tinted non-white surface alpha 0.64-0.82, proof-title >=16px/650 weight, source-tag >=12px, evidence-snippet >=13px, result seal main text 20-28px/800 weight. Never use pale low-opacity text for evidence.
evidence_chain.anti_card: Proof nodes must not be ordinary white cards, card panels or independent tiles. They should look like rail-attached material anchors: a small numbered dot, a source-tag, a short evidence snippet and a connector to the rail. Avoid rgba(255,255,255,*), #fff/#f8fafc/neutral gray fills, box-shadow, full rectangle borders and large rounded rectangles.
evidence_chain.proof_node_visual: Each proof-node must choose exactly one allowed structure and include its modifier class: spine_label uses proof-node--spine-label + proof-anchor-spine; bracket_anchor uses proof-node--bracket-anchor + rail-attached-bracket; cut_corner_tag uses proof-node--cut-corner-tag + proof-material-chip. Do not invent other proof-node structures. Bind each proof-node to proof_node_bboxes by data-proof-id and keep the wrapper fully inside that bbox. Each proof-node must include proof-title, source-tag and evidence-snippet. The visual surface height must be >=72px and >=62% of the mapped proof_node_bboxes height; if using percentage height inside evidence-flow, height must be >=62%, never 17%-30%. proof-title font-size >=16px and weight >=650; source-tag >=12px; evidence-snippet >=13px. Shorten copy instead of shrinking text. Connectors and decorative spines/brackets must be short and inside the bbox or evidence rail only: use left:0/top:0 or positive inset values, never left:-4px or negative pseudo-element offsets. Result seal must stay inside its bbox with non-negative left/top/width/height; rings, icons and glow belong inside SVG viewBox padding, not CSS negative offsets. Use colored/tinted non-white surfaces, no box-shadow, radius 0-8px, no full four-side border, and no card/panel/tile/box class names.
evidence_chain.special: If no real image is available, evidence anchors look like material snippets/log cards with source-tag, not empty screenshot placeholders. If evidence anchors exceed 4, fold extra sources into a slim source strip.

metric_dashboard.layout: One hero metric dominates; 2-4 support metrics and one chart/trend/composition explain it.
metric_dashboard.sizes: Hero metric numeral 54-88px; support metric numeral 30-44px; chart area at least 28% body area.
metric_dashboard.connectors: Charts need axis/category labels or explicit legend. Do not use decorative fake bars without meaning.
metric_dashboard.special: If exact data is weak, show qualitative trend/level and source label instead of fake precision.

comparison_matrix.layout: Use mirror comparison, before-after bridge or 2x2 matrix. Axes/dimensions must be explicit.
comparison_matrix.sizes: Column width 180-310px; row height 56-88px; winning side 1.1-1.25x stronger by fill/stroke/scale.
comparison_matrix.connectors: Central bridge arrow 4-6px if showing upgrade. Keep row separators subtle.
comparison_matrix.special: If text is dense, keep only row labels + short deltas; move explanations to notes.

timeline.layout: Use milestone rail, stair-step or roadmap band. Each milestone shows order/time plus output.
timeline.sizes: Milestone nodes 130-210px by 58-92px; rail 4-6px; current/key milestone 1.15x larger.
timeline.connectors: Clean rail, no crossing vertical lines. Output tags sit above/below rail with 12-24px gap.
timeline.special: If more than 6 milestones, group into phases and show 3-5 phase nodes.

risk_matrix.layout: Use 2x2 matrix, response lanes, shield layers or control loop. Encode level by position/size/color.
risk_matrix.sizes: Risk cell 150-230px by 70-110px; response band height 54-84px; shield layers 64-96px.
risk_matrix.connectors: Trigger to response arrows 2-3px. Avoid alarm red covering the whole page.
risk_matrix.special: Each risk needs trigger + response. If missing, show checkpoint/status rather than inventing.

value_loop.layout: Use ring/cycle/hub-spoke. Central value or final destination is largest.
value_loop.sizes: Center node 220-340px by 100-150px; loop nodes 130-190px by 56-86px; outcome tags 90-140px by 28-42px.
value_loop.connectors: Cycle arrows 3-5px, evenly spaced. Max 6 loop nodes.
value_loop.special: If actors >6, group into platform/user/partner/resource clusters.

semantic_infographic.layout: Choose exactly one metaphor: ring, matrix, tower, stage or split compare.
semantic_infographic.sizes: Main visual at least 45% body area; support labels max 4.
semantic_infographic.connectors: Use minimal explicit relations. No random decorative network.
semantic_infographic.special: If unsure, use focus statement + 3 support groups + result badge.

technical_route.when_to_use: Research plan, implementation route, technical route, methodology sequence, project path.

extract_schema.topic_name: Project or research topic name, or summarize from content.

render_contract: Diagram type: technical route map.
Use 3-6 route stages. Each stage must contain action + method/result label.
Use a clear beginning and ending. The final result node must be visually stronger.
If methods and contents are parallel, show them as side bands feeding into the main route.
Use standard flowchart shapes: rectangle for stage, rounded rectangle for method, diamond for decision/validation.
Feedback loop, if present, must be one dashed arrow only.

flowchart.when_to_use: Operational steps, execution process, demo flow, data handling sequence, problem solving steps.

extract_schema.feedback_loop: Source and target of feedback, optional.

render_contract: Use 3-6 main nodes. Do not exceed 6.
Use stable structures: horizontal flow, vertical flow, swimlane, or loop.
Decision nodes must be diamonds, max 2.
Connectors must be short, clear and mostly straight. Use one dashed feedback arrow only.
Nodes should align on a grid. One node may be emphasized, but the structure cannot collapse into random cards.
Evidence labels must sit near related steps, not on the connector line.

architecture.when_to_use: System structure,端-边-云, modules, platform layers, technology stack, deployment topology.

extract_schema.layers: 3-5 layers, ordered from source/device to application/user.
extract_schema.boundary: System boundary, external systems, user/device side.

render_contract: Show layers and boundaries first; modules are secondary.
Use horizontal or vertical bands, tower, or hub-spoke. Avoid equal horizontal step chain.
Data flow arrows must show direction from source to value.
Keep modules inside their layer boundary. No floating modules.
If there are many modules, group them into clusters rather than drawing all nodes.
Highlight one output value or core capability as the visual destination.

data_flow.when_to_use: Data collection, cleaning, storage, analysis, query, feedback, pipeline pages.
render_contract: Make the data path visually continuous. Use one strong line or band.
Separate source, processing, storage/model and output by bands or lanes.
Quality control labels should attach to the exact processing step.
Use feedback arrow only when page content explicitly supports feedback.
The output/result zone must be the final focal point.

evidence_chain.when_to_use: Proof, verification, demo evidence, screenshots/logs/results proving a claim.

extract_schema.claim: What has been proven, 12-24 Chinese chars.
extract_schema.evidence_sources: 2-4 sources, e.g. log, screenshot, benchmark, field record.
extract_schema.evidence_actions: What was done to produce evidence.
extract_schema.evidence_results: What result each evidence item proves.
extract_schema.missing_asset_policy: Whether image slot or generated asset is needed.

render_contract: Start with the claim. The claim must be the first visual reading point.
Use 2-4 evidence anchors. Each anchor must include source + action/result.
Evidence anchors may look like material cards, logs, small dashboard pieces or photo crops, but not upload boxes.
If using a path, use one simple arrow from evidence to value. No wave chains.
Final value/action must be visibly connected to the claim.

metric_dashboard.when_to_use: KPIs, metrics, performance, experimental result, efficiency/cost/accuracy pages.

extract_schema.main_metric: The one metric that must dominate.

render_contract: One main metric must be visually dominant. Do not make four equal KPI cards.
Every metric needs unit or source context.
Secondary metrics must support the main conclusion.
If drawing a chart, include axis/label logic; do not use decorative fake charts.
Use a bottom or side interpretation label to state what the metric means.
forbid: decorative chart with no data meaning

comparison_matrix.when_to_use: Before/after,方案对比, pain point vs solution, old vs new, option selection.
render_contract: Axes or comparison dimensions must be explicit.
Use alignment and contrast to show difference quickly.
Highlight the winning/target side, but keep comparison credible.
Use short row labels. Avoid paragraph cells.
If there is an upgrade path, show a central arrow or bridge.

timeline.when_to_use: Development history, project plan, milestones, phased implementation.
render_contract: Timeline must show time/order and output, not only event names.
Use 3-6 milestones.
The current or key milestone should be emphasized.
Outputs may sit below/above the rail as short tags.
Keep rail clean. Avoid many crossing vertical lines.

risk_matrix.when_to_use: Risk, safety, exception handling, quality control, security pages.
render_contract: Risk level must be visually encoded by color, size or position.
Each risk needs trigger + response, not just a name.
Use matrix, lanes, shield layers or loop. Avoid plain tables.
The controlled-state conclusion should be visible.
forbid: alarm colors covering the whole page

value_loop.when_to_use: Value creation, business closed loop, ecological relationship, stakeholder loop.
render_contract: Put central value in the center or final destination.
Use ring/cycle/hub-spoke. Nodes must be evenly spaced.
Show exchange direction with simple arrows.
Use 2-4 outcome labels around the loop.
The loop must explain why the system improves over time.

pyramid.when_to_use: Capability hierarchy, maturity model, layered goals, from foundation to outcome.

extract_schema.levels: 3-5 hierarchy levels from foundation to top.
extract_schema.transition_logic: How lower level supports upper level.

render_contract: Use 3-5 layers. Wider foundation, narrower top.
Top goal must be visually clear.
Layer labels should be short and centered.
Side callouts may explain evidence, max 3.
Use consistent layer spacing and no overlapping text.

radar.when_to_use: Capability dimensions, maturity evaluation, multi-dimensional comparison.
render_contract: Use 4-6 axes only.
Labels must be outside the radar, not overlapping the polygon.
Highlight strongest and weakest dimensions with callouts.
If exact scores are unavailable, use qualitative levels instead of fake precision.

route_map.when_to_use: 推广路径, regional deployment, rollout plan, market route, implementation path.
render_contract: Use route, map, road or stage-gate metaphor.
Route must have a visible destination.
Each stage should include condition + result.
If no real map is available, use abstract map/road, not fake geography.
Destination/result node should be emphasized.

semantic_infographic.when_to_use: Fallback when no specialized diagram type fits.
render_contract: Choose one simple visual metaphor and commit to it.
Do not fall back to equal card grid.
Use one focal statement and 2-4 support labels.
Keep relationships explicit with minimal lines.
